corrections.original: Every loop-free McCulloch-Pitts net corresponds to a logical expression and vice versa.
corrections.fix: Converse holds only for logical expressions 'satisfying certain conditions' (abstract); for any such expression a net can be found.

corrections.original: 1943 paper byline: University of Illinois College of Medicine, Illinois Neuropsychiatric Institute (only).
corrections.fix: Byline also names 'The University of Chicago'.

corrections.original: Cybernetics sold over 22,000 copies by end of 1949 [cited to historyofinformation.com and Wikipedia].
corrections.fix: Figure confirmed but those sources do not contain it; it comes from Kline, The Cybernetics Moment (2015), via IEEE T&S review. Source replaced.

corrections.original: Turing proposed educating a child machine with rewards and punishments.
corrections.fix: Add Turing's caveat: rewards and punishments 'can at best be a part of the teaching process'.

corrections.original: The chess prediction came true only in 1997, 39 years late.
corrections.fix: 1997 is 39 years after the 1958 prediction but 29 years after its 1968 ten-year deadline.

corrections.original: UNVERIFIED: Simon, 1965: 'machines will be capable, within twenty years, of doing any work a man can do.'
corrections.fix: Verified from scans: Simon, The New Science of Management Decision (1960), p. 38: '. . . machines will be capable, within twenty years, of doing any work that a man can do.' Date is 1960 (reprinted 1965). Promoted to verified quotes.

corrections.original: Whether Logic Theorist was running on a computer during Dartmouth is contested (Cordeschi Aug 1956 vs 1957 runs).
corrections.fix: Accounts are compatible: first JOHNNIAC proof August 1956; 38/52 results from late-1956/1957 runs. Newell and Simon were scheduled only for the first two weeks, so it was not running during their visit. The 'arrived with a working program' line is the error.

corrections.original: Pitts, a self-taught runaway who never earned a degree.
corrections.fix: Smalheiser (2000) says he never held degrees of any kind; Wikipedia (citing Godel Collected Works) says Chicago awarded him an Associate of Arts. Film-safe: 'never finished a doctorate'.

corrections.original: The workshop ran about eight weeks, roughly 18 June to 17 August 1956.
corrections.fix: Eight weeks per Solomonoff/More notes; six weeks traditional (Nilsson); the Rockefeller Foundation calls it 'five-week'. Film-safe: 'one summer, about two months'.

corrections.original: SNARC had about 300 vacuum tubes (Minsky) vs 3,000 (AIMA).
corrections.fix: Kept as contested; Minsky's own 1981 words ('three hundred tubes', 'nearly three hundred tubes', six per neuron x 40) support ~300.

corrections.original: Von Neumann on Minsky's thesis: 'If it isn't now, it will be someday.'
corrections.fix: No primary source; not in the Bernstein excerpt checked. Keep as UNVERIFIED — do not use as a quote.

corrections.original: Minsky 1982: 'The AI problem is one of the hardest science has ever undertaken.'
corrections.fix: Only second-hand via Ellen Ullman (2005) per Quote Investigator; original 1982 source unidentified. Keep UNVERIFIED.

corrections.original: Wiener on Pitts: 'without question the strongest young scientist whom I have ever met.'
corrections.fix: Reported by Gefter without the primary letter. Use only as reported speech.

corrections.original: Pitts wrote to Russell about errors in Principia and Russell invited him to Cambridge.
corrections.fix: Biographical tradition (Gefter after Conway & Siegelman); no surviving letter cited. Present as 'the story goes'.

corrections.original: In 1974 McCarthy told McCorduck: 'I won't swear that I hadn't seen it before' [cited to a Substack summary].
corrections.fix: Full wording: 'I won't swear that I hadn't seen it before - a vague memory that someone else had used the word' (1974 recorded interview for Machines Who Think). The audio is in McCorduck's CMU papers with restricted access, so it is second-hand. Use only as reported speech, not as a voiced quote.
